\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সুদ} (sud)}{সুদ (sud)}]{\bn{সুদ} (sud) — interest (on money)}

\label{lesson:BN-C415-sud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a cheque, then the Bengali for cash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সুদ}}
\textbf{\bn{সুদ}} — \emph{sud} — \textquotedblleft{}interest (on money)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ব্যাংক} \bn{সঞ্চয়ের} \bn{ওপর} \bn{সুদ} \bn{দেয়।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bængk sôñchôyer opôr sud dey.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bank pays interest on savings.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সুদ}} (\emph{sud}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{sūd}, \textquotedblleft{}profit, gain, interest\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sud}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sud}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bængk sôñchôyer opôr sud dey.} — The bank pays interest on savings.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a cheque, then the Bengali for cash, then say \emph{sud} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সুদ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Interest (on money)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পাসবই} (pāsbôi)}{পাসবই (pāsbôi)}]{\bn{পাসবই} (pāsbôi) — a passbook (for a bank account)}

\label{lesson:BN-C415-pasboi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for cash, then the Bengali for interest (on money).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পাসবই}}
\textbf{\bn{পাসবই}} — \emph{pāsbôi} — \textquotedblleft{}a passbook (for a bank account)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাবা} \bn{পাসবই} \bn{খুলে} \bn{সুদের} \bn{টাকা} \bn{দেখলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bābā pāsbôi khule suder ṭākā dekhlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father opened the passbook and looked at the interest.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পাসবই}} (\emph{pāsbôi}) joins English \emph{pass}, from \emph{passbook}, to the Bengali \textbf{\bn{বই}}, \textquotedblleft{}a book\textquotedblright{}: half borrowed and half translated.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāsbôi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāsbôi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bābā pāsbôi khule suder ṭākā dekhlen.} — Father opened the passbook and looked at the interest.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for cash, then the Bengali for interest (on money), then say \emph{pāsbôi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পাসবই} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A passbook (for a bank account)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{লেনদেন} (lenden)}{লেনদেন (lenden)}]{\bn{লেনদেন} (lenden) — transactions; dealings (in money)}

\label{lesson:BN-C415-lenden}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for interest (on money), then the Bengali for a passbook.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{লেনদেন}}
\textbf{\bn{লেনদেন}} — \emph{lenden} — \textquotedblleft{}transactions; dealings (in money)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আজ} \bn{ব্যাংকে} \bn{অনেক} \bn{লেনদেন} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āj bængke ônek lenden hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There were a lot of transactions at the bank today.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{লেনদেন}} (\emph{lenden}) pairs \bn{লেন}, \textquotedblleft{}taking\textquotedblright{}, built on \textbf{\bn{নেওয়া}}, to take, with \bn{দেন}, \textquotedblleft{}giving\textquotedblright{}, built on \bn{দেওয়া}, to give: taking and giving, the whole business of money.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lenden}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lenden}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āj bængke ônek lenden hôlô.} — There were a lot of transactions at the bank today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for interest (on money), then the Bengali for a passbook, then say \emph{lenden} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{লেনদেন} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Transactions; dealings (in money)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করা} (biniyog kôrā)}{বিনিয়োগ করা (biniyog kôrā)}]{\bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করা} (biniyog kôrā) — to invest}

\label{lesson:BN-C415-biniyog-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a passbook, then the Bengali for transactions.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{biniyog kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to invest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অরুণ} \bn{তার} \bn{সঞ্চয়} \bn{একটা} \bn{ব্যবসায়} \bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ôrun tār sôñchôy ekṭā bæbsāy biniyog kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Arun invested his savings in a business.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{জমিতে} \bn{টাকা} \bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini jômite ṭākā biniyog kôrlen}.

The noun alone is \bn{বিনিয়োগ}, an investment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{biniyog kôrā}) joins Sanskrit \emph{viniyoga}, \textquotedblleft{}apportioning, putting to use\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), to \bn{করা}, to do; the money sense is the modern one.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{biniyog kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{biniyog kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôrun tār sôñchôy ekṭā bæbsāy biniyog kôrlô.} — Arun invested his savings in a business.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a passbook, then the Bengali for transactions, then say \emph{biniyog kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To invest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{খোয়ানো} (khoyāno)}{খোয়ানো (khoyāno)}]{\bn{খোয়ানো} (khoyāno) — to lose (money or property); to forfeit}

\label{lesson:BN-C415-khoyano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for transactions, then the Bengali for to invest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{খোয়ানো}}
\textbf{\bn{খোয়ানো}} — \emph{khoyāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to lose (money or property); to forfeit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ব্যবসায়} \bn{অরুণ} \bn{তার} \bn{সব} \bn{সঞ্চয়} \bn{খোয়াল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bæbsāy ôrun tār sôb sôñchôy khoyālô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Arun lost all his savings in the business.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{সব} \bn{টাকা} \bn{খোয়ালেন}, \emph{tini sôb ṭākā khoyālen}.

\bn{হারানো} is to lose anything, a key or the way; \bn{খোয়ানো} is to lose what you had of value, often by your own doing.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{খোয়ানো}} (\emph{khoyāno}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{khoyā}, \textquotedblleft{}thrown away, lost\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{kṣapita}, \textquotedblleft{}cast away, destroyed\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3653).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khoyāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khoyāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bæbsāy ôrun tār sôb sôñchôy khoyālô.} — Arun lost all his savings in the business.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for transactions, then the Bengali for to invest, then say \emph{khoyāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{খোয়ানো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To lose (money or property); to forfeit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Rented Rooms to Interest and Investment}

\label{lesson:BN-R415-review-408-415}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for a rented home and a tenant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a rented home, a tenant, an advance (payment), a security deposit, to reside
  \item an area, a slum, a housing colony, a resident, to hang out (chatting)
  \item an open ground, a park, a courtyard, a square (open place), to pace up and down
  \item a post office, an office, a letter (sent by post), a postman, to send
  \item a boundary wall, a gate, a brick building, a lamp post, to climb over
  \item a drain, a pipe, a dustbin, dirt, junk
  \item a bank (for money), a counter, a cashier, a cheque, cash
  \item interest (on money), a passbook, transactions, to invest, to lose (money or property)
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A rented home? (\textbf{\bn{বাসা}}, \emph{bāsā}.) A tenant? (\textbf{\bn{ভাড়াটে}}, \emph{bhāṛāṭe}.) An advance (payment)? (\textbf{\bn{অগ্রিম}}, \emph{ôgrim}.) A security deposit? (\textbf{\bn{জামানত}}, \emph{jāmānôt}.) To reside? (\textbf{\bn{বসবাস} \bn{করা}}, \emph{bôsbās kôrā}.) An area? (\textbf{\bn{এলাকা}}, \emph{elākā}.) A slum? (\textbf{\bn{বস্তি}}, \emph{bôsti}.) A housing colony? (\textbf{\bn{কলোনি}}, \emph{kôloni}.) A resident? (\textbf{\bn{বাসিন্দা}}, \emph{bāsindā}.) To hang out (chatting)? (\textbf{\bn{আড্ডা} \bn{দেওয়া}}, \emph{āḍḍā deoyā}.) An open ground? (\textbf{\bn{মাঠ}}, \emph{māṭh}.) A park? (\textbf{\bn{পার্ক}}, \emph{pārk}.) A courtyard? (\textbf{\bn{উঠোন}}, \emph{uṭhon}.) A square (open place)? (\textbf{\bn{চত্বর}}, \emph{chôtvôr}.) To pace up and down? (\textbf{\bn{পায়চারি} \bn{করা}}, \emph{pāychāri kôrā}.) A post office? (\textbf{\bn{ডাকঘর}}, \emph{ḍākghôr}.) An office? (\textbf{\bn{অফিস}}, \emph{ôphis}.) A letter (sent by post)? (\textbf{\bn{চিঠি}}, \emph{chiṭhi}.) A postman? (\textbf{\bn{পিয়ন}}, \emph{piyôn}.) To send? (\textbf{\bn{পাঠানো}}, \emph{pāṭhāno}.) A boundary wall? (\textbf{\bn{পাঁচিল}}, \emph{pā̃chil}.) A gate? (\textbf{\bn{গেট}}, \emph{geṭ}.) A brick building? (\textbf{\bn{দালান}}, \emph{dālān}.) A lamp post? (\textbf{\bn{ল্যাম্পপোস্ট}}, \emph{læmpposṭ}.) To climb over? (\textbf{\bn{টপকানো}}, \emph{ṭôpkāno}.) A drain? (\textbf{\bn{নর্দমা}}, \emph{nôrdômā}.) A pipe? (\textbf{\bn{পাইপ}}, \emph{pāip}.) A dustbin? (\textbf{\bn{ডাস্টবিন}}, \emph{ḍāsṭbin}.) Dirt? (\textbf{\bn{ময়লা}}, \emph{môylā}.) Junk? (\textbf{\bn{জঞ্জাল}}, \emph{jônjāl}.) A bank (for money)? (\textbf{\bn{ব্যাংক}}, \emph{bængk}.) A counter? (\textbf{\bn{কাউন্টার}}, \emph{kāunṭār}.) A cashier? (\textbf{\bn{ক্যাশিয়ার}}, \emph{kæshiyār}.) A cheque? (\textbf{\bn{চেক}}, \emph{chek}.) Cash? (\textbf{\bn{নগদ}}, \emph{nôgôd}.) Interest (on money)? (\textbf{\bn{সুদ}}, \emph{sud}.) A passbook? (\textbf{\bn{পাসবই}}, \emph{pāsbôi}.) Transactions? (\textbf{\bn{লেনদেন}}, \emph{lenden}.) To invest? (\textbf{\bn{বিনিয়োগ} \bn{করা}}, \emph{biniyog kôrā}.) To lose (money or property)? (\textbf{\bn{খোয়ানো}}, \emph{khoyāno}.)
